clue.text: Conservative in frivolous manoeuvre

indicators.note: one thing placed in another means the first word's letter sits inside the second word

explanation.surface: A Tory politician caught up in some flippant political scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside JOKEY to give JOCKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To jockey is to manoeuvre for position, as riders do when jostling during a race.

clue.text: Enlisted, being coherent

definitions.meaning: first meaning: signed up for the armed forces

explanation.surface: A recruit who has signed up and is talking sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Joined up as two words means enlisted; hyphenated it describes thinking or writing that hangs together.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined-up thinking is integrated and consistent, and someone who joined up became a soldier.

clue.text: Prisoner with search for occupation

parts.note: a quest is a long search

explanation.surface: An inmate looking around for a job to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' reads as a job, but here it means the taking over of territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is the seizure and military takeover of a land, which is an occupation of it.

clue.text: Icon? Judge one after protest without depth

indicators.note: depth is abbreviated as one letter, which must be dropped from the protest word

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether to rule on a symbol after a shallow demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Icon' suggests a religious image, but the question mark points to the little pictures used in text messages. Depth is abbreviated D.
explanation.definitionFit: An emoji is a small pictorial icon used in text messages; the question mark flags this modern, digital example.

clue.text: Revolutionary objections, given life, becoming persistent

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the objections word is read backwards

parts.note: to be born is to be given life

explanation.surface: Radical complaints that come alive and refuse to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means obstinately persistent, unwilling to give up or change course.

clue.text: Arrangement of minuet is great, giving indication of rhythm

indicators.note: a musical arrangement rearranges a piece, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Praise for a musical arrangement of a minuet that marks the beat well.
explanation.definitionFit: A time signature is the pair of numbers at the start of a stave showing beats per bar, the music's metre.

clue.text: Reports, learner admitted, restricted by coach?

indicators.note: something restricted is hemmed in, so the coach word encloses the rest

parts.note: a coach is a kind of bus
L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Reports of a novice let onto a team but held back by the trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a trainer, but the question mark warns it is the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulletins are short official news reports or statements issued to the public.

clue.text: Flower kept by porch ideally

indicators.note: the answer is held within the following words, kept across their join

explanation.surface: A bloom that would ideally be grown on a porch.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchid is an exotic plant prized for its elaborate blooms.

clue.text: Fall asleep? Certainly not with party very loud

explanation.surface: Nobody could doze off with such a noisy party going on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that nobody sleeps through a loud party; FF is the musical mark for fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod off is to drift gradually into sleep, often unintentionally.

clue.text: Great cricketer getting on a bit, wildly theatrical player

indicators.note: acting wildly means behaving without order, so the preceding letters are scrambled

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: An ageing sporting great who has become a wildly theatrical performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Botham is a famous England cricket all-rounder of the 1970s and 80s.
explanation.definitionFit: Botham was one of England's finest all-rounders, a celebrated star of the sport.

clue.text: Elated, settle project and dance

parts.note: to land is to come to rest
to project is to throw, or fling

explanation.surface: In high spirits, finishing off a scheme and then dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' and 'project' read as finishing a scheme, but both are verbs of motion here. The Highland fling is a lively Scottish solo dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a traditional Scottish dance performed with energetic hops and kicks.

clue.text: Note odd parts of creeds intertwined

parts.note: the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the odd-numbered positions of the next word are the ones to keep

explanation.surface: Remarking that bits of various faiths are woven together.
explanation.definitionFit: Laced means threaded together or interwoven, as laces are passed through eyelets.

clue.text: Avoiding noise in electronic projection

parts.note: E abbreviates electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: one item placed in another means the noise word goes inside the rest

parts.note: a lug is a projecting handle or ear
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Steering clear of the hum from a piece of electronic equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projection' suggests a cinema screen, but here it is a physical part that sticks out, like a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eluding means escaping or evading something, so it is a synonym for avoiding.

clue.text: Officer repeated phrase after woman

parts.note: a riff is a repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: An official who speaks after a woman, echoing her words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After woman' places the riff after SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheriff is a law enforcement official, chief peace officer of a US county.

clue.text: Usual rule newly broken by good, popular science fiction writer

indicators.note: something broken and made anew has its parts reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A familiar convention overturned by a well-liked writer of science fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: G and IN join the letters of 'usual rule' before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursula Le Guin was the American author of the Earthsea books and The Left Hand of Darkness.

clue.text: Clues all over the place about main character being lustful

indicators.note: going round something means these letters surround the next piece
scattered everywhere means the letters of the preceding word are jumbled

parts.note: the hero is the lead character

explanation.surface: Muddled hints surrounding a protagonist who turns out to be a lecher.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecherous describes someone with excessive or offensive sexual desire, a synonym of lustful.

clue.text: Simple holding company I had set up, undistinguished

indicators.note: the simple word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: mere means nothing more than, simple

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: A plain firm that I once founded, which never stood out.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means only ordinary or average in quality, lacking anything remarkable.

clue.text: Raised cases involving obstinate type lacking energy and incentive

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the cases word encloses the next piece
in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the word for cases is backwards
energy is abbreviated as one letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: Lawsuits brought against a tired, stubborn person with an incentive.
explanation.walkthrough: MULE loses its E (energy) and sits inside STIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus is something that spurs action or effort, an incentive or encouragement.

clue.text: Survey held as designed by alien for sensational publication

indicators.note: something designed is newly arranged, so the preceding letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A survey drawn up by an extraterrestrial for a lurid tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal sheet is a newspaper specialising in gossip and sensationalised stories.

clue.text: Bear cost of offer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be able to pay for
second meaning: provide, as in giving an opportunity

explanation.surface: Paying for what is on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford is both to have enough money for something and to provide or supply it.

clue.text: Expression of surprise over gardener's latest story after loss of a shrub

indicators.note: the story word loses its single letter a
the latest letter is the final one of the gardener's word

explanation.surface: A gardener's tale of a lost bush, told with astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' in a down clue puts MY on top of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Myrtle is an evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers and glossy leaves.

clue.text: Rush revision of a file without one blank page

indicators.note: a revision reworks text, so the letters are reordered
one is the Roman numeral I, which goes missing

explanation.surface: Hurrying to revise a document with a page left empty.
explanation.walkthrough: A FILE drops its I before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A flyleaf is the blank sheet at the start or end of a book, attached to the cover.

clue.text: Element in place of education probed by artist with doubtful expression

indicators.note: something probed has another thing pushed into it

explanation.surface: A painter quizzing a hesitant student about a chemical element at university.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is the radioactive metallic chemical element with atomic number 92.

clue.text: Stumble, not following convert

indicators.note: following is abbreviated as one letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: A wobbly believer who no longer follows a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in 'p. 10f'.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change it, so convert and alter are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Better time secured by old pair in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters run backwards
something secured is held fast inside the following letters

explanation.surface: An elderly retired couple who have a better time of it now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here, not a comparison. O + DUO is reversed to OUDO, then T goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or beat them, which is to better them.

clue.text: Exactly the same dialect in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so these letters are dispersed and regrouped

explanation.surface: A regional way of speaking heard unchanged on radio or television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means alike in every detail, with no difference whatsoever.

clue.text: Daughter with resolution wise to get equestrian training

parts.note: res is the abbreviation for resolution, as on a screen

explanation.surface: A determined, sensible daughter who signs up for riding lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' reads as determination but supplies its abbreviation RES.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the training of a horse to perform precise movements, also a competitive horse-riding discipline.

clue.text: Limits abandoned by bishop giving commands

indicators.note: abandoned means left behind, so the bishop letter leaves the word

explanation.surface: A bishop issuing instructions to drop the restrictions.
explanation.definitionFit: To order is to instruct with authority, so commands as a verb means the same thing.
